title: Shots Fired at Ammy Virk's Convoy After Canada Concert, Singer Escapes Unhurt
excerpt: Abbotsford police are investigating after multiple rounds were fired at a vehicle in the Punjabi singer-actor's convoy following his concert in British Columbia on September 5.
body:
• A vehicle in Ammy Virk's convoy was fired upon in Abbotsford, British Columbia, shortly after his concert on September 5, with reports suggesting seven to ten shots were fired.
  • No injuries were reported. Multiple accounts identify the targeted vehicle as a bulletproof Rolls-Royce Cullinan carrying four people.
  • A burnt-out SUV was found about five kilometres from the shooting, and police are investigating whether the two incidents are connected.
  • Virk briefly posted an Instagram statement saying he was "completely fine" and not involved, then deleted it within minutes.

Punjabi singer and Bollywood actor Ammy Virk was reportedly caught in a shooting incident in Abbotsford, British Columbia, on the night of September 5, shortly after wrapping up a concert at Rogers Forum during his 2026 Unity Tour.

According to multiple reports, occupants of a dark-coloured SUV opened fire on a vehicle in Virk's convoy around 11 p.m. as it travelled along the 2500-block of McCallum Road. Accounts from local Indo-Canadian media and event organisers suggest between seven and ten shots were fired at the vehicle, striking its rear window.

Bulletproof Vehicle Shielded Passengers

Several reports identified the targeted vehicle as a bulletproof Rolls-Royce Cullinan carrying four people, including Virk and the concert promoter. The vehicle's armour reportedly prevented the bullets from penetrating, and no injuries were sustained by anyone inside.

Event organisers were quoted in Indian media confirming that Virk was inside the vehicle at the time of the shooting, though Abbotsford Police have not independently verified the identities of the occupants, citing privacy concerns.

Burnt SUV Adds New Dimension

Shortly after the shooting, police received a separate report of a vehicle fire in the 2400-block of Sunnyside Place, roughly five kilometres away. Officers arriving at the scene found an SUV completely engulfed in flames. Investigators are now examining whether the torched vehicle is linked to the shooting.

The Abbotsford Police Department's Major Crime Unit has taken over the investigation and described the shooting as appearing to have been targeted, though no motive has been established and no arrests have been announced.

"Preliminary information indicates that individuals in a dark-coloured SUV fired multiple shots at the victim vehicle."

— Abbotsford Police Department statement

Conflicting Statements Cloud the Picture

On September 9, Virk posted an Instagram Story on his official handle stating he was "completely fine" and urged people not to believe everything being "reported or circulated." He wrote, "Waheguru di Meher naal I'm completely fine and I was not involved in any such reported or suggested incident." The post was deleted within minutes of appearing.

Virk's father, Kuljit Singh, the sarpanch of Lohar Majra village in Nabha, told reporters that the firing was not directed at his son's vehicle but was instead linked to the party that had organised the show. "He has no enmity with anyone," Kuljit Singh said, adding that the family had confirmed Ammy was safe.

Rising Safety Concerns for Touring Artists

The Abbotsford incident was not the only disruption during Virk's Canadian tour. Earlier in the week, his Toronto concert was reportedly disrupted by a separate disturbance involving audience members.

Virk, who has appeared in Bollywood films including 83, Bad Newz and Khel Khel Mein, is one of Punjabi music's biggest touring acts. Canada is home to one of the largest Punjabi diaspora communities in the world, making it a critical market for artists from the industry.

Police have appealed for dashcam footage from the McCallum Road area between 10:45 p.m. and 11:30 p.m. on September 5, and from Sunnyside Place between 11 p.m. and midnight. The investigation remains ongoing.
image_caption: Punjabi singer and actor Ammy Virk. Shots were fired at his convoy after a concert in Canada, though the singer was unharmed.
nri_angle: The incident raises safety concerns for Indian performers touring abroad, particularly in Canada where the Punjabi diaspora forms a major concert audience.
